problem: If the sum of the first $20$ terms of an arithmetic series is ${S}_{20}=301,$ and the common difference is $d=1.5,$ then the first term of the series is ${a}_{1}=${{field-1}}.

feedback.problem: What is the first term of an arithmetic series if the common difference is $d=-2,$ and the sum of the first $20$ terms is ${S}_{20}=-160?$
feedback.worked_solution:
We are given the common difference of the series. So, to find the first term, we use the formula for the sum of an arithmetic series in the form

$$
{S}_{N}=\frac{N}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(N-1)d),
$$

where ${a}_{1}$ is the first term, $d$ is the common difference, and $N$ is the number of terms.

Substituting $N=20$, $d=-2$, and ${S}_{N}=-160$ into the formula above, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-160 & =\frac{20}{2}(2{a}_{1}+(20-1)(-2)) \\ -160 & =10(2{a}_{1}-38) \\ -16 & =2{a}_{1}-38 \\ 22 & =2{a}_{1} \\ {a}_{1} & =11.\end{aligned}
$$
